hook_ideas: A spacecraft launched before most of your viewers were born is still sending data from 25 billion kilometers away — but every year its power fades.
The 'Pale Blue Dot' — a photo of Earth as a tiny speck — was taken at the request of Carl Sagan, and it changed how we see ourselves.
Voyager 1 has left the solar system, but it's still not truly 'out' — it's in interstellar space, but still within the Sun's gravitational influence.
The Golden Record: a time capsule for aliens — but no one knows if it will ever be found.
misconceptions: Voyager 1 has left the solar system — actually, it has exited the heliosphere but is still within the Sun's gravitational sphere of influence (the Oort Cloud).
Voyager 1 is the fastest human-made object — that record is held by the Parker Solar Probe, which reaches much higher speeds near the Sun.
Voyager 1's nuclear power 'runs out' soon — it's not a nuclear reactor but RTGs, and they decay gradually, but the spacecraft is expected to operate until around 2025-2030 for science data.
